title: Checkpoint format breadcrumbs (safetensors + sharding)
content:
High-level: debugging intermittent load failures when we pull customerX/modelY (HF) into Dedicated pools. Failures only show up on ~1-2% of requests; reproduces locally when streaming shards over flaky network. Notes + commands I ran, error snippets, quick hypotheses and next steps.

Observed symptoms:
- Crash during torch.load or safetensors load when model is sharded (8 shards). Usually after the download completes but sometime while streaming.
- Errors: RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading bytes; EOFError: Ran out of input; safetensors.errors.InvalidFileError: magic header not found; AssertionError: expected 65536 bytes got 4096
- When failure occurs, size of local shard file is smaller than expected (truncated). Sometimes manifest/index.json lists correct sizes but actual bytes are short.

Commands / repro steps I tried:
1) HF snapshot download (repro with and without caching):
   huggingface-cli snapshot-download customerX/modelY --revision=main --cache-dir ./hf_cache_test
   -> sometimes snapshot-download exits successfully but one of the bin shards is truncated (smaller filesize).

2) raw HTTP download with curl and range to simulate streaming problem:
   curl -L -o pth-00001-of-00008.bin "https://huggingface.co/customerX/modelY/resolve/main/pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin" \
     --write-out "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n" --fail --retry 3 --max-time 120

3) s3 copy (customer stored a copy in S3 for us):
   AWS_PROFILE=customerX aws s3 cp s3://customerx-models/modelY/pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin ./local/ --no-progress --only-show-errors
   -> sometimes aws reports full size but sha256 differs from the hf-hosted copy.

4) quick integrity checks:
   sha256sum pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin
   stat -c%s pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin
   hexdump -C pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin | head -n5
   python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; print(list(safe_open('pth.safetensors').keys()))"  (for safetensors)

5) tried loading with torch to see error context:
   python - <<'PY'
import torch
try:
    st = torch.load('pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin', map_location='cpu')
    print('loaded ok')
except Exception as e:
    import traceback; traceback.print_exc()
PY

Error snippets captured:
- RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading bytes (expected 8192 more bytes)
- EOFError: Ran out of input
- safetensors.errors.InvalidFileError: magic header not found
- ValueError: file size does not match header (declared 123456789, actual 123441234)
- During model load: RuntimeError: Error(s) in loading state_dict for LlamaForCausalLM: Missing key(s): "lm_head.weight". Unexpected key(s): "module.lm_head.weight" (when DDP wrapper mismatch)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Server-side packaging bug: index.json or manifest lists full shard sizes but the object storage returned truncated stream under certain keep-alive / chunked encodings. Nginx proxy or CDN edge is returning early on connections with particular TLS ciphers.
2) Client-side streaming logic: huggingface-cli / requests library may not be checking Content-Length consistently for chunked responses; partial file written and rename completed too early.
3) Artifact replication mismatch: customer pushed two slightly different versions to different backends (S3 vs HF) and index points to different blob.
4) safetensors vs pytorch binary confusion: Some shards are published as safetensors but named .bin; loader mismatch causes magic header errors on attempt to load with torch.load.
5) Checksum/manifest bug in upload tooling (git-lfs or hf-upload) that truncated objects >100MB when using a proxy.

What I changed / temporary mitigations tried:
- Added explicit content-length verification after download: compare header Content-Length vs downloaded bytes; keep retry if mismatch. Script:
   curl -sI URL | grep -i Content-Length
   curl -L URL -o tmp && [ $(stat -c%s tmp) -eq $CONTENT_LENGTH ] || exit 1
- Switched huggingface-cli to use --use-auth-token (to avoid anonymous CDN paths) — seemed to lower failure rate but not eliminate.
- For Dedicated nodes, changed downloader to use ranged GET + reassemble (download in 8MB chunks, verify each chunk). This reduces occurrence in local tests.
- Added post-download sha256 verification step and fail-fast on mismatch. Customer will need to publish checksums if we want deterministic detection.

Notes about sharding conventions that bit us:
- Two common conventions: pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin (plain binary shards, load with torch.load -> state_dict shards merged) vs. safetensors shards: model.safetensors, model-00001-of-00008.safetensors. Some publishers mix naming.
- HF now also supports index.json referencing shards; if index.json is stale it points to old shard names/sizes.

Repro script (simple) to force failure locally by truncating stream:
- Run a local nginx that serves shards but kills connection after N bytes to simulate CDN behavior. Then run snapshot-download and observe loader errors. (I used nginx with chunked transfer disabled.)

Next actionable items / TODOs:
- [ ] Add robust post-download checksum verification into redwoodctl artifact fetch flow (redwoodctl download --verify-sha256).
- [ ] Ask infra/team to replicate nginx chunked-edge truncation: spin up proxy with keepalive timeout and run hf snapshot-download under load (JIRA: JIRA-ML-981).
- [ ] Request customer to publish per-shard sha256 in model card or index metadata for deterministic checks.
- [ ] Add CI test: simulate truncated shards and assert loader reports clear error (not segfault / mis-merge).
- [ ] For safetensors vs torch mismatch: detect file magic header before selecting loader. magic bytes for safetensors: b'SAFE' in header, check first 8 bytes.

Scratch commands to reuse later:
- Inspect HF URL headers: curl -sI "https://huggingface.co/customerX/modelY/resolve/main/pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin"
- Download with retries & verify: 
  URL=... ; EXPECTED=$(curl -sI $URL | sed -n 's/Content-Length: //Ip' | tr -d '\r') ; curl -L $URL -o tmp || exit 2 ; [ "$(stat -c%s tmp)" = "$EXPECTED" ] || (echo mismatch && exit 3 )
- Quick safetensors header check: python - <<PY
with open('shard.bin','rb') as f:
    print(f.read(8))
PY

Random notes and guesses:
- We see more failures from certain client IP ranges (maybe old ISP / MTU fragmentation?). Could be small windows where chunked-encoding + TLS interaction causes early EOF.
- When a file is truncated but still contains valid footer bytes, torch.load sometimes reports Missing/Unexpected keys instead of corruption — misleading error. Need to map these cases.
- We should prioritize clear, deterministic detection (file-size, sha256) before passing shard files to loader.

If anyone else hits this, copy/paste this doc, add a short repro and attach the truncated shard (I put one small truncated sample in: /tmp/riley_trunc_sample.bin).

Appendix: useful references I pinged/checked:
- HF snapshot-download docs + known issues: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/using-snapshot-download
- safetensors python package: https://github.com/huggingface/safetensors
- Our infra PR that changed download retry logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/452

End of breadcrumbs.
